headline: KSE-100 claws back over 460 points on fresh US-Iran de-escalation hopes, while Fauji Cement posts its best-ever year.
summary: KSE-100 bounced 464.53 points (+0.26%) to 180,311.21 on Wednesday, clawing back part of Tuesday's 1,463-point slide, as hopes of a US-Iran de-escalation firmed up again. Banks led the recovery (HBL, MCB, MEBL, NBP, UBL all among the day's named gainers), and Fauji Cement (FCCL) posted its best-ever annual profit, Rs16.2bn, with a fresh Rs1.50/share dividend declared. The external backdrop stays calm (georisk score 38/100) but oil is up 7% this month and the rupee is drifting weaker, so the desk leans constructive but not carefree — one bad Iran headline already erased 1,100 points earlier this week.

risks: Headline whipsaw on US-Iran diplomacy — the same story that knocked 1,463 points off the index on Tuesday put over 460 back on Wednesday; a single bad statement can reverse the week.

Oil and the rupee are both leaning the wrong way at once: Brent +7% this month and USD/PKR at 277.49 (+0.23% 1mo) feed imported inflation and keep SBP hawkish, a headwind for OMCs, refiners and exporters.

Gold's 11.9% one-month rally is a safe-haven signal (georisk factor stress 75) — if that flight-to-safety bid keeps building, it's a sign global risk appetite for frontier markets like PSX could cool.
